summary:
Main
The three things business investors need to know about this week's artificial intelligence (AI) rout:
While some of the issues are idiosyncratic to Nvidia's governance, the outcome of the US election has opened the issue of the broader social costs of AI development. Markets are beginning to price in the eventuality of slower AI development. While risks are real, potential delays in AI projects could be an opportunity for investors, firms and the economy to adapt.

# Years of Polling Shows Overwhelming Voter Support for a Crackdown on AI

*AnyAlawmakerAalignedAwithAAIAandABigATechAisAonAtheAwrongAsideAofApublicAopinion.A*

### Public Citizen | April 2026

American voters in both parties overwhelmingly oppose AI's development and deployment, support aggressive regulation or prohibition of AI, and reject efforts to stop state-level regulation of AI, especially to protect kids online. These findings are consistent across <u>dozens of polls</u> conducted over the past decade - with public opinion turning even more sharply against AI and Big Tech in the last few years, as AI company recklessness and abuses have become more evident.
